transcription.text: A honeybee colony functions through highly specialized roles that allow thousands of insects to behave as a coordinated system. The queen lays eggs, workers gather food and maintain the hive, and male drones have a narrower reproductive role. Worker bees perform demanding tasks throughout short lives, while new generations continually replace those that die. Communication and division of labor allow the colony to regulate food, temperature, and care for developing bees. Studying the hive shows how cooperation among individuals can produce behavior that is more complex than the actions of any single bee.
